# SE-1S: source actually generated by the emitted channels

Declared before calculation, 20 September 2026. Analyze the first eight
completed SE-1 cases (through sign-mirror), using their immutable final states.
This is a diagnostic of the existing equations, with no new fit or evolution.

For X,Y only, at fixed canonical fields, momenta, gradients and vector A,
differentiate their Hamiltonian density with respect to the background U:

    D = 2 a (Pi_X^2+Pi_Y^2) - 2 beta dot J_XY
        + mass2 [chi r^2 - kappa_U X r],
    r = Y-kappa X.

The scalar momentum source from these terms is -g D. Report the integrated
signed D, positive/negative parts, kinetic, shift, and mixing contributions,
the full X/Y propagation plus mixing energy, and their ratio when nonzero.
Do not equate this instantaneous inhomogeneous ratio to SE-1M's phase-averaged
homogeneous eigenmode coefficient. No eigenmode-population claim is made.

Independently verify the integrated derivative by perturbing U uniformly by
1e-7 in an independently assembled X/Y Hamiltonian, holding all canonical
states fixed. Require absolute error <=1e-9 +1e-5 abs(D). Also require the
assembled energy to match archived X+Y+mixing terms within 1e-12. Zero-channel
controls must give zero energy and source within 1e-12. Sign-mirror source and
energy must agree with exchange-200 within 1e-10 absolute plus 1e-8 relative.

Record spherical shell integrals for radii [0,1,2,3,4,infinity] in model units,
including signed and absolute source. Do not infer an inverse-square force or
a lens from these integrals; the full candidate field equations must propagate
them. Record U extrema and matter internal-energy change alongside the result.
Use every declared case, including negative source coefficients and failures.
Pin code before execution; archive source/state hashes and source commit.

Decision: does enhanced local response coexist with appreciable self-generated
source in the actual short spatial evolution? Even a positive answer does not
prove a physical fuel budget, late-time stability, orbit or observational fit.
Hamiltonian differentiation and spherical integration are established math;
the constitutive functions belong to the declared candidate.
